title: Canary quota misattribution — Acme Financial overage appeal
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Acme Financial reported a 48-hour unexpected invoice delta after a canary rollout of quota sharding changes. The customer claims the platform billed duplicate tokens for requests that retried across regions. Initial support triage found spikes in per-tenant token meters coincident with the canary deployment window (2026-03-09 02:00–06:00 UTC). This ticket tracks the investigation, remediation, and crediting actions for the overage appeal.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy canary routing rules that split tenant traffic across quota-shards. 2) Simulate intermittent upstream failure to trigger client retries. 3) Observe meter events emitted by rate-limiter service and shard-allocator. 4) Confirm if duplicate meter increments occur when requests are retried and handled by different shard instances.
investigation_notes:
- Correlated meter increase with canary window using billing dashboard (Grafana dashboard: billing/tenant-metering-rate).
- Found ~2.1k duplicate meter events for tenant acme-fin on 2026-03-09 02:12–02:18 UTC. Query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM meter_events WHERE tenant_id='acme-fin' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-03-09T02:00Z' AND '2026-03-09T03:00Z' GROUP BY event_hash;
- Root cause: shard-allocator introduced ephemeral shard IDs during canary; retrying client requests carried original request IDs but no consistent shard affinity header. Rate-limiter keyed on combination {tenant, shard_id, request_id} but the shard_id changed between initial request and retry, causing two separate meter increments.
- Edge condition: gateway retry logic attaches X-Retry-Count but did not preserve X-Shard-Affinity for canary shards; cross-region proxy (eu-west edge) forwarded retry to a different shard pool (us-east) which used a new shard_id.
- Telemetry gaps: missing correlation IDs in meter_events for ~12% of retries.
action_items:
- Hotfix #1: Modify rate-limiter to deduplicate on a canonical request fingerprint (tenant + request_id + canonical_shard_affinity) — PR created. (ENG-17427 follow-up)
- Hotfix #2: Gateway to preserve X-Shard-Affinity across retries; fallback to request_id if header absent.
- Monitoring: Add alert on per-tenant duplicate-meter-rate > 0.1% for 5m.
- Rollback: Revert canary shard ID generation to stable-ID strategy until audit completed.
- Credits: Calculate and issue customer credit for confirmed duplicate-billed tokens; coordinate with billing ops.
- Postmortem: Draft root-cause and share with customers and legal.
resolution_summary: Applied immediate hotfix to rate-limiter dedup logic and patched gateway to preserve shard affinity on retries. Rolled the canary back to stable-ID strategy at 2026-03-09 08:20 UTC. Confirmed duplicate-meter events reduced to baseline within 15 minutes. Billing ops issued a pro-rated credit to Acme Financial for $12,342.50 covering the confirmed duplicate counts after verification. Postmortem draft linked below.
credits_issued: $12,342.50 (confirmed duplicate-token billing window: 2026-03-09 02:12–02:18 UTC). Credit processed by billing-ops invoice-id INV-2026-03-9876.
acceptance_criteria:
- Duplicate-metering event rate for acme-fin returns to baseline (<0.01%) for 48 hours after fixes.
- Automated dedupe unit tests covering request_id+shard changes added to rate-limiter CI.
- Customer acknowledgment received and credit applied.
- Postmortem published and remediation tickets scheduled.
